phase1_dag.equation: Gamma_k = g_hi + rho * x_hi * M ;  pass iff Gamma_k < 0

A0.why: Lemma Dv': min(Abar, tau/D_lo); tau/D_lo binds on the tail

Abar, tau, C_T, D_lo, D1, D2.why: Arb/FLINT operator registry REGISTRY_C2 (and C1); certified, operator_only, rule r2

Lambda (lower bound on E_a[tau]).why: C4 theorem L for 306-308; C7 PRIMARY for 309. Enters ONLY as an admissibility FLOOR on A0 via Lemma SM(d). It is NOT an input to Gamma.

M.why: max(|lo|,|hi|) over the TC-T enclosure. The sealed clause also clips against the R2 interval; neither that interval nor M_R2 is carried in any committed artifact, so the clip is UNREACHABLE and is dropped. Dropping it can only RAISE Gamma, so every threshold here is at least as demanding as the sealed one, and the clip does not bind at any of the 20 committed supplies.

g_hi.why: R_interval.hi - e0 * D_interval.lo; recovered exactly from the committed (Gamma_exact, M_after_exact) pair and cross-checked against all five committed supplies per cell

order-3 surrogate.why: the frozen TC-T rule accepts an `order3` argument; no certified order-3 value exists for the tail cells. Its effect IS quantified in committed evidence as Gamma_perfect_order3.

rho.why: cell half-width (e_hi - e_lo)/2, from REGISTRY_C2 blocks

x_hi.why: cell right endpoint e_hi, from REGISTRY_C2 blocks

phase2_gap_anatomy.A_pointwise_Lambda_e_lo: C7 certifies Lambda(e_lo) >= 3.586306093865 for cell 309, and C4 certifies analogous pointwise bounds for 306-308.
phase2_gap_anatomy.B_uniform_sup_over_cell: sup_{e in cell} Lambda(e) >= Lambda(e_lo). NOT certified.
phase2_gap_anatomy.C_tau_prime: the alarm time of the unclipped pathwise majorant; tau >= tau' pathwise.
phase2_gap_anatomy.D_tau: the true CUSUM alarm time; E[tau] >= E[tau'].
phase2_gap_anatomy.E_operator_A0: A0 = min(Abar, tau/D_lo), a certified UPPER bound on sup_cell E_a[tau].
phase2_gap_anatomy.F_consumed_by_C5T_K5B: Gamma consumes A0, A1, A2 through M only.
phase2_gap_anatomy.THE_CENTRAL_STRUCTURAL_FACT: Lambda is a LOWER bound on E_a[tau] and A0 is an UPPER bound on the same quantity. Gamma depends on A0, never on Lambda. Lambda enters the decision ONLY as the floor below which no admissible A0 can go. Therefore any route that improves Lambda -- which is exactly what R1 and R2 do -- RAISES the floor and can never lower Gamma. R1 and R2 cannot close a cell. They can only strengthen an EXCLUSION, which is what C7 did.
exact_inequalities: Lambda(e_lo) <= sup_{e in cell} E_a[tau]            (a point is at most the sup)
sup_{e in cell} E_a[tau] <= A0                       (Lemma SM(d) admissibility)
hence  Lambda(e_lo) <= A0  for every admissible A0   (the FLOOR)
phase2_gap_anatomy.role_of_Lambda_309: Lambda_309 is a FEASIBILITY DIAGNOSTIC for the operator route, not an input to the closure clause. It answers 'how small could a perfect A0 ever be?'. When it exceeds the A0 ceiling the clause can tolerate, the operator route is refuted for that cell.

which_inequality_causes_which_gap.G1_clipping: E[tau'] <= E[tau] -- C7 bounds E[tau'], so Lambda understates E[tau]. Closing it RAISES Lambda.
which_inequality_causes_which_gap.G2_uniformization: Lambda(e_lo) <= sup_cell -- C7 is pointwise. Closing it RAISES Lambda.
